summary: Penghao Sun works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. Sun studied under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Qingying Chen, Weirong Shen, Mark Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Peter K. Bol, Jay Jasanoff, James Robson, Ryuichi Abe, Jie Li, and Borjigidai Oyunbilig.
Penor 02 studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and also taught Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé.

Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Palyul Monastery and under Thubten Chökyi Dawa, Karma Tekchok Nyingpo, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Jampel Gyepai Dorje. In 1978, he founded Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.

Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1935–1949) under Gustaf John Ramstedt and served there as Docent of Comparative Linguistics (1958–1980).

Per Kjeld Sørensen (b. 1950) studied Tibetology at the University of Copenhagen (1971–1982, ~1980–1990) under Erik Haarh. He lectured at Copenhagen (1982–1989), held a fellowship at the University of Bonn (1991–1992), and was a professor at the University of Leipzig (1994–2017).

Per Kvaerne (b. 1945) works in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed a Ph.D. at the University of Oslo by 1973 and later held posts there as a professor (attested 1978, 1991–1996) and served as Secretary General of the IATS.

Per Kværne (b. 1945) studied Sanskrit at the University of Oslo (Mag. art. ~1965–1970, Dr. phil. ~1970–1973). He lectured at the University of Bergen (1970–1975) and served as Professor at the University of Oslo (1975–2007).

Peri Bhaskararao (b. 1947) is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Professor of Phonetics and Phonology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1986–1998) and held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1998–2012).
Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Wilhelm Rau (~1967–1971) and held a post at the University of Marburg (~1971–1991).

Perry Link (b. 1944) is a sinologist who earned a B.A. at Harvard University (~1962–1966). He held posts at Princeton University (1973–1977), UCLA (1977–1988), and the University of California, Riverside (~2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel (b. 1954) studied and completed his habilitation at the University of Munich (~1977–1996). He held posts at Munich, Innsbruck, Salzburg, the University of Glasgow (2000–2009), and the University of Münster (2009–2023).

Peter Adamson (b. 1972) is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied at Williams College (~1990–1994) and the University of Notre Dame (~1994–2000), later holding posts at King's College London (~2000) and the University of Munich (~2012).

Peter Alan Roberts is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed doctoral research supervised by Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich.

Peter C. Bisschop studied Indology and religious studies at the University of Groningen (PhD -2004) under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He was a Fellow at Wolfson College, Oxford, and taught Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010).

Peter Connolly works in religious studies and Indology. He completed his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and was appointed Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock (b. 1958) studied at Yale University and under traditional teachers Seungsahn Haengwon and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim. He served as Director of the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center (attested 2007–2013).
Peter Dronke (1934–2020) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Magdalen College (~1955–1958) and held a post at the University of Cambridge from approximately 1961 to 2001.
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.

Peter Fenner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held a post at Deakin University. He studied under advisers Noble Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, as well as traditional teacher Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche.

Peter Francis Kornicki (b. 1950) studied at Oxford (Lincoln and St Antony's colleges), Tokyo University of Education, and under Masamichi Asukai and Mitsukuni Yoshida. He taught at the University of Tasmania (1978–1982), Kyoto University (~1982–1985), and the University of Cambridge.
